articles.title: Fender Creates Special Pokemon Guitars
articles.intro: This lesson covers Fender’s special edition Pokemon guitars for the 30th anniversary, their features, and how they celebrate classic Pokemon games.

sentences.text: In 1996, Game Boy players in Japan began their Pokemon adventures with the games _Pokemon Red_ and _Pokemon Green_.
Now, 30 years later, Pokemon Red and Green are back — but as guitars!
Guitar company Fender has released two special electric guitars in Japan for Pokemon's 30th anniversary.
And you can probably guess what colors they are!
The two guitars are based on different Fender guitars: the red guitar is a Stratocaster, and the green version is a Telecaster.
Both are among the company's best-known electric guitars, played by people like Buddy Holly, Jimi Hendrix and Keith Richards.
In the Pokemon games, red is often associated with Fire-type Pokemon, while green is associated with Grass types — so each guitar is also covered in lots of pictures of Pokemon from these two groups.
The fretboard of each guitar even has little Poke Balls as fret markers!
And if you push the top of the volume knob, the guitar adds a fuzz effect that makes it sound like 8-bit music, like the type used in those first Pokemon games.
Each guitar also comes with 11 red or green picks, each with different Pokemon characters.

The guitars each cost {{prn:396,000|three hundred and ninety six thousand}} yen — or about {{prn:$2,500|two thousand and five hundred dollars}} — and there's no information yet about how many will be sold.
For now, they're only being sold through a lottery to people in Japan.
People can enter the lottery through the Pokemon Center Online store in Japan between November 19 and November 24.

articles.title: Sleeping in on Weekends May Be Bad for Your Heart
articles.intro: This lesson explores research linking irregular sleep schedules, like sleeping in on weekends, to a higher risk of heart problems.

sentences.text: After a busy week, staying up late on Friday and sleeping in on Saturday can feel like a well-earned reward.
But according to new research, that reward might not be so good for your heart.
A team of researchers from Harvard Medical School studied sleep data from more than 10,000 American adults who wore activity trackers for around six months.
In total, the data included over one million nights of sleep.
The researchers looked at how long people slept, when they went to bed and woke up, how much time they spent in different sleep stages, and how their sleep schedules changed from night to night.
They then followed the participants for almost four years to see whether they had heart problems.

The study — which has not yet been peer reviewed — found that people whose sleep schedules changed from night to night over the six-month period had a 20% to 23% higher risk of problems such as heart attacks, strokes and heart failure.
And every 29-minute change in how long they slept from one night to the next  — whether sleeping more or less — was linked to a 24% higher risk of these problems.
Study researcher Nguyen Minh Tuan Viet said that while people often focus on getting a full eight hours of sleep each night, keeping a regular sleep schedule is a simple way to protect heart health.
So, the next time you're tempted to stay up late on Friday night, remember that keeping to your usual bedtime might actually be a better reward for your heart.

articles.title: China's Workers Now Support More Elderly than Children
articles.intro: Explore China’s rising elderly population, changing dependency ratios, and the social and economic effects of an aging society.

sentences.text: Newly released data from China's National Bureau of Statistics has shown that, in 2025, for the first time, the country's old-age dependency ratio surpassed its child dependency ratio.
The old-age and child dependency ratios are used to estimate the burden placed on a country's working-age population by those too old or too young to work.
The old-age dependency ratio takes the number of people aged 65 and above and compares it to the number of people of working age — here defined as those aged 15 to 64.
Meanwhile, the child dependency ratio compares the number of children 14 and younger to the working-age population.
The higher the ratio, the more old or young people are, theoretically, being supported by the working population — though these figures don't actually count who is working and who is not.
China's old-age dependency ratio has been rising for some time, going from 15% in 2016 to 21% in 2021.
And in 2025, it rose to 23%, while the child dependency ratio was 22%.
It's the latest indicator of China's aging population and the economic impacts that may accompany it.
It was already estimated that there were more elderly people than children in China for the first time in November 2025.
While China's aging population has been precipitated by a variety of factors, one major cause was the country's one-child policy, which limited most families to having just one child.

This limit was in place between 1980 and 2015, and while it played a big part in reining in population growth, it also resulted in there now being fewer young people to support the growing elderly population.
Now, although the one-child limit has been removed, higher living costs and changing expectations for men and women's roles in society mean the country's birth rate has continued to fall.

Experts warn that China's aging population could limit the country's economic growth, and force the government to spend more on pensions and long-term healthcare while spending less on families and education.

articles.title: Travelers Want 'Plot Twist Trips' to Show Their Wild Side
articles.intro: Explore the rising trend of "plot twist trips," where travelers seek surprising, out-of-character adventures and unique vacation experiences.

sentences.text: Emily loves city breaks.
She loves going to the spa, eating in nice restaurants and drinking wine with a beautiful view of the city.
But Emily's next vacation is a hiking trip in the jungle.
She'll be sleeping in a tent, eating basic food, and she probably won't shower for a few days.
Nobody would have ever imagined Emily would go on a trip like that — and that's the point!
"Plot twist trips" are among Booking.com's top travel predictions for 2027, according to a report by the travel platform.
The report looked at opinions from more than 28,000 travelers around the world to find out what travel trends are most likely to be popular next year.
The results showed that 77% of travelers would like to choose a vacation specifically to do something "completely out of character."
Booking.com said that, in a world of algorithms and constant connection, "plot twist trips" can help people take a break from the predictability of everyday life.
Around two-thirds of travelers said they want their next trip to surprise them in some way.
And 36% are hoping to get a reaction from their friends and family by sharing pictures of themselves doing something out of the ordinary on their trip!
Another possible trend for 2027 is "social currency" — choosing whom to travel with based on whether they budget the way you do.
Half of travelers in the report said they've reconsidered inviting certain people on trips because of differences in budgets or spending habits.
And many more people may be choosing their next vacation based on "vibes," according to the report.
Eighty-one percent of travelers said they would choose a vacation not based on what they want to see, but how they want to feel.
And how some people may want to feel is scared — because almost two-thirds said they're interested in travel experiences that are paranormal in some way!

articles.title: 4 in 10 UK Teens Want More Work Experience at School
articles.intro: This lesson explores a survey of UK teens who want more work experience, financial skills, and job guidance at school.

sentences.text: More than 40% of UK teenagers want more opportunities for work experience at school, with a similar percentage asking for more guidance on how to apply for jobs, a survey done for the _BBC_ has found.
The online survey included 2,000 young people aged 13 to 18.
They were asked for their thoughts on how school can better prepare them for employment and adult life.
Along with the 44% who said they would like more work experience opportunities in school, 43% also said they would like to learn how to manage their finances.
Forty-two percent said they want more guidance on how to apply for jobs, and 39% said they want to learn more about managing stress and mental health.
Thirty-eight percent also said they'd like help improving their communication skills.

The survey was done as part of this year's Teen Summit event, which was hosted at Newcastle College — a secondary school — where students were given a chance to talk more about their thoughts and experiences.
Many students at the event talked about their worries about money.
For example, Ella, whose second name was not shared, talked about how expensive it is to go to university, with students needing to pay around $13,000.
She added that even her entrance exam cost about $100.
"I have to get a job because I can't afford all of this," she said.
Speaking about the event, Newcastle College student Elliot Smith said, "It was a really great experience hearing from people my own age about the challenges they're facing."
He also said he liked having the chance to share his own thoughts.

articles.title: Special Suits Could Make Japan's Castles More Accessible
articles.intro: Explore how special suits are helping make Japan's historic castles more accessible for wheelchair users and visitors.

sentences.text: Japan has lots of castles, but getting to them isn't always easy.
Visitors sometimes have to climb hundreds of steps, and some castles aren't accessible at all to people who can't walk.
However, that may soon change!
A few years ago, a company called Techno Associates created a type of "suit" that makes it easier to walk and climb.
And last month, the city of Hikone decided to test whether these suits could help make Hikone Castle more accessible for wheelchair users.
However, the suit is really more of a set of straps worn over clothes.
It uses air pressure to provide extra support to the back and legs, reducing the effort needed to move.
They're not strong enough to help wheelchair users walk — but they can make it easier to carry them.
Hikone Castle is one of only 12 castles in Japan where the main tower is still standing.
And getting there isn't easy — there are about {{prn:140|one hundred and forty}} steps to the top.
So, on October 19, city employees and volunteers wore Techno Associates' suits to help them carry wheelchair users up to the top.
The wheelchair users sat in a wooden palanquin, which was held up by a long bar across two of the carriers' shoulders.
The suits helped the carriers support the weight as they climbed the steps.
Each team had six people, who took turns carrying the palanquin.
The carriers said the suits were very helpful on the climb, making it a lot easier to carry the palanquin.
The city is thinking of using this not only as a way to help wheelchair users visit the castle, but also as a way to let visitors experience being carried around like the nobility were in the past!
It could also be a way to make castles around Japan more accessible.

articles.title: KDDI Plans Drone Deliveries for Lawson Products
articles.intro: Explore Japan's plans to use drones for delivering Lawson convenience store products and the impact on daily life, logistics, and disaster relief.

sentences.text: What's that in the sky?
Is it a bird?
Is it a plane?
No, it's your grocery delivery!
Starting in 2027, food and everyday essentials could be flying through the skies above Japan, with customers in some parts of the country getting their orders delivered by drone.
And products from Lawson convenience stores could be among the items making the journey.

Japanese telecommunications company KDDI and its drone business, KDDI Smart Drone, have announced that they will be working with Wing, an American drone delivery company owned by Google's parent company, Alphabet.
The companies announced their plans at the end of October.
They hope to start the service in some areas of Japan next year, before expanding to more locations.
The service could be especially useful for people who find it difficult to visit shops.
In Japan, around 9 million people have trouble buying groceries because their age makes it difficult to get around, or due to a lack of nearby stores.
So these drone deliveries could help them get food and other products without leaving home.
The service could also save time for busy families that struggle to fit shopping into their daily lives.
And with Japan facing a shortage of delivery drivers, drones could help reduce pressure on delivery companies.
As well as delivering groceries to customers, the companies also believe these drones could help deliver important supplies during disasters.
Wing already has plenty of experience with drone deliveries.
The company has completed more than 1 million drone deliveries, and makes thousands of deliveries every day in the US.
Its drones can deliver orders within 30 minutes, bringing products directly to customers' gardens or other chosen locations.
KDDI, meanwhile, has experience with mobile networks and drone operations in Japan.
If the plans go ahead, looking up at the sky could soon mean spotting someone's dinner on its way home!

articles.title: New 'Blue Zone' of Long-Lived People Found in Sardinia
articles.intro: Discover how researchers identified a new "blue zone" in Sardinia, where people live unusually long and healthy lives.

sentences.text: If you want to know where people live the longest, look no farther than our planet's "blue zones."
"Blue zones" are areas where people live unusually long, healthy lives.
There are only six of them around the world, including Okinawa in Japan and the Greek island of Ikaria — while Singapore was just added to the list in 2023.
The first blue zone was identified on the Italian island of Sardinia in 2004 — a cluster of mountain villages in the eastern part of the island.
Now, 22 years later, researchers believe they may have found a second blue zone on Sardinia — a village called Bolotana in the center of the island, about 110 kilometers from that first blue zone.
Researchers studied the village between 2021 and 2025.

During this time, the village had a population of about {{prn:2,300|two thousand and three hundred}} people, among whom 10 were aged 100 or older — putting the proportion of centenarians at 442 out of {{prn:100,000|one hundred thousand}}.
Okinawa, meanwhile, now has {{prn:1,192|one thousand one hundred and ninety two}} centenarians — giving it a proportion of 81 out of {{prn:100,000|one hundred thousand}}.
The researchers found that men who reached the age of 70 in Bolotana had an average life expectancy of 16 more years, while for women it was almost 21 more years.
And 5% of 70-year-old men even survived until they were 100 — while 14% of women did the same.

Looking to explain why people in Bolotana might enjoy such longevity, the researchers found that the local diet is about 90% plant-based, with people mostly producing their own food, and meat eaten only about five times a month.
The village is also very hilly, and few people have cars, so everyone gets lots of exercise just walking around every day.
But while women globally generally live three to five years longer than men, the researchers aren't sure why women in Bolotana are so much more likely than men to reach 100!

articles.title: 70% of Japanese Kids Read Less than an Hour a Week
articles.intro: This lesson explores a survey revealing that most Japanese children spend less than an hour a week reading books and how parents influence their habits.

sentences.text: Watching videos, playing games or reading books — which do you prefer?
For many children in Japan, books aren't their first choice, even if they enjoy reading.
A new survey by the Hakuhodo Foundation's Child Research Institute asked 1,200 elementary and junior high school students about their reading habits.
The survey found that just under 70% of children like reading books — however, over 70% spend less than an hour a week reading books, and some don't read at all.
In fact, about three out of four children said watching videos or playing video games is more fun than reading.
And books seem to become less popular as children get older.
Junior high school students are less interested in reading than younger children, and they also spend less time actually reading books.
However, the survey found something interesting about children who love reading — their parents often have a love of books too!
In families where parents read for at least an hour a week, more than 90% of children say they like books.

And compared with other parents, those whose children love reading are more likely to give their children books about their interests, read aloud to them, and regularly take them to libraries and bookstores.
So videos and games may be more popular with many children, but books haven't lost their place.
And parents may help keep that love of reading alive!

articles.intro: This lesson discusses whether bringing an iced coffee to a job interview is appropriate, exploring opinions and workplace culture differences.

sentences.text: You're a manager and you're meeting a new job candidate.
She's got lots of experience and she's very polite.
But in her hand is an iced coffee, which she brings into the interview.
As a manager, how would you feel about this?
This question has been dividing the internet for a few months.
It began in September, with a TikTok video posted by a US recruiter with 16 years of experience.
In the video, the recruiter said she had noticed a lot of younger candidates going into interviews with iced coffees in hand.
She said bringing an iced coffee to an interview makes it seem like the interview is "just a stop on your list of errands for the day."
She finished the video by telling people not to take iced coffee into interviews with them, adding that it "just looks like you didn't have time to finish your coffee."
The video quickly got people talking.
Some agreed with the recruiter, saying that job interviews should be formal.
Some said candidates should try to look as professional as possible, and that going in with an iced coffee could make it seem like the candidate isn't taking the interview seriously.
Others thought the recruiter was being too strict, with some saying that rejecting a candidate because of an iced coffee says more about the interviewer than the candidate!
So, should you bring an iced coffee to an interview?
It might depend on the interviewer or the type of job you're interviewing for — more relaxed working environments might not have a problem with it.
But if you're not sure how formal the interview will be, it might be best to finish your coffee before the interview — or, at least, ask the interviewer if it's all right to bring it in with you.

articles.title: teamLab to Open Digital Art Museum in US
articles.intro: Learn about teamLab's first US digital art museum, its unique immersive exhibits, and the OC Vibe district opening in Anaheim, California.

sentences.text: teamLab has come a long way since it was founded in Tokyo in 2001.

Famous for its immersive artworks that explore the meeting points between art, science, technology and nature, its works are exhibited in museums all around the world, and its own museums in places like Tokyo and Kyoto are major tourist attractions.
Now, teamLab is opening its first permanent museum in the US.
The new museum will be part of a new sports and entertainment district called OC Vibe, which is being built in the city of Anaheim, in Orange County, California.
"teamLab Museum Anaheim" is the tentative name for the new facility, which will have a floor space of around 10,000 square meters.
A raised walkway will connect the museum directly to the Anaheim Regional Transportation Intermodal Center, which is the train and bus station for the area.
And on the other side of the museum, just across the freeway, is Angel Stadium, home of the Major League Baseball team the Los Angeles Angels.
The design for the new museum has been done by architecture firm Smith-Clementi, which also created the plans for the rest of the OC Vibe district.

Because teamLab's immersive exhibits require a windowless building, the architects have designed the exterior as a "shimmering cloak" with scales that catch the light and change color at different times of day, according to the OC Vibe website.
Anaheim's teamLab museum will add a major art facility to the OC Vibe district, which will also include parks, offices, restaurants, hotels, apartments and a concert hall.
OC Vibe will begin opening its facilities in 2027, and the teamLab museum is set to open in 2030.

articles.title: Petting Your Dog May Protect You from Future Stress
articles.intro: Explore a study on how petting your dog before stressful events may help reduce future stress and improve your stress response.

sentences.text: If you know that life is about to get more stressful, petting your dog might be the preparation you need to make it easier to manage.
A study published in _Biological Psychology_ looked at how interacting with their pets affected dog owners' responses to stress.
The research included 64 dog owners, who took their pets to the researchers' lab while they did a stress test.
During the stress test, the participants had their heart rate and brain activity monitored.
There were two parts to the stress test.
In one, participants had to answer general knowledge questions with a short time limit.
The other part was an arithmetic task, with participants being asked to count backward following a set pattern and pace.
To add extra stress, the participants were told they were being video recorded, and someone gave them negative feedback when they got things wrong.
Between doing the two parts of the stress test, the participants were given a five-minute break, during which they sat on a chair in a room with their dog.
The dog was either free to move around the room and go to their owner, or kept on a short leash and out of reach.
Unsurprisingly, the general knowledge and arithmetic tests caused signs of physical stress among participants, including increased heart rates and brain activity linked with feeling tense.

And while you might expect that interacting with their dog would help participants calm down, the stress levels of participants who could pet their dog during the recovery period didn't drop any faster than those who couldn't reach their dogs.
But participants who could pet their dog did show lower levels of stress during the second part of the test.
This suggests that physical contact with their pet had a buffering effect for the stress they were about to experience.
So if you've got a stressful day ahead, be sure to pet your dog now — not later!

articles.title: Japan's Anime Market Hits Record $28.2 Billion
articles.intro: Explore how Japan's anime industry hit a record $28.2 billion, driven by international growth, hit titles, and challenges like piracy.

sentences.text: Spending on Japanese anime reached a record 4.45 trillion yen — about $28.2 billion — in 2025, up 15.8% from the previous year, according to new figures from the Association of Japanese Animations (AJA).

The preliminary findings of the _Anime Industry Report 2026_ were presented on October 30 at TIFFCOM, an entertainment industry event held as part of the Tokyo International Film Festival, with the full release expected in December.
The 4.45 trillion yen figure includes total spending on anime films, TV shows, streaming, merchandise and live events in 2025.
It marks the first time the market has passed 4 trillion yen, with annual growth also reaching a record high.
Overseas sales rose 17%, while domestic sales climbed 14%.
This was a big change from 2024, when overseas sales jumped 26%, but domestic growth was much slower, at just 5%.
Both domestic and overseas sales were helped by the huge success of _Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — Infinity Castle_, which became the highest-grossing Japanese film of all time.
Japanese anime now also make up 100 of IMDb's top 300 user-rated animated TV series.
_Attack on Titan_ tops the list, while _Death Note_ ranks third and _One Piece_ ninth.
"It is no longer unusual for anime to be ranked among the top-performing box office or streaming titles overseas.
It is safe to say anime has achieved a breakthrough in the international market," said Masahiro Hasegawa, the report's editor-in-chief.
As the industry continues to grow internationally, AJA says companies will need to adapt their content and business practices to different languages, cultures and laws.
It also said online piracy is an important problem to address.
Japan's government has set a goal of increasing overseas anime sales to 6 trillion yen, or about $38 billion, by 2033.

articles.title: Democrats Win US House and Senate
articles.intro: Explore how Democrats captured both chambers of the US Congress, voter frustrations, diverse historic wins, and the impact on President Trump's term.

sentences.text: Democrats have won control of both chambers of the US Congress, as voters expressed their dissatisfaction with Washington under the control of Republicans and President Donald Trump.
The country's November 3 midterm elections exposed voters' frustrations over high prices, the Iran war and concerns over government corruption.
Democrats won across the map, flipping states that had voted Republican for decades and that Trump won easily just two years ago.
That includes James Talarico's Senate victory in Texas, where no Democrat had won statewide office in more than 30 years.

The election also delivered the country's first Muslim senator, first Native American female senator and first openly gay male senator, as well as the country’s first Black female governor and first Native female governor.
Young people and Latinos, who helped return Trump to the White House two years ago, are now moving away from Republicans, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of midterm voters in all 50 states.

The AP Voter Poll also showed that about three-quarters of voters feel "angry" or "dissatisfied" with the country's direction, while about 6 in 10 see Trump as prioritizing his personal interests over those of the country.
The president's failure to deliver on key promises — particularly to reduce inflation, which has worsened instead — also held back his fellow Republicans.
Democrats increased their support with moderate voters, particularly in key Senate races where Democrats flipped Republican-held seats.
About 8 in 10 moderate voters said Congress was not doing enough to provide checks and balances on the president.
It was all a major blow to Trump, who spent nearly every day of the last month speaking in front of supporters, telling voters to "pretend I'm on the ballot."
As the results came in, Trump blamed individual Republican candidates for their losses, though he also said Democrats "did a good job."
Trump now faces a very changed Washington for the last two years of his presidency.
Democrats will have the power to block laws he supports, reject his choices for key positions and investigate his government.

articles.title: Japan Launches New Agency to Deal with Disasters
articles.intro: Learn about Japan’s new disaster agency, its role in preparing for future earthquakes, tsunamis, and how it aims to improve emergency shelters.

sentences.text: Japan has launched a new disaster management agency to improve the country's preparedness for major earthquakes, tsunamis and volcanic eruptions.
The National Disaster Management Agency, which began operating on November 2, has more than 350 staff members responsible for disaster preparedness, emergency response and reconstruction efforts.
Japan, which lies along the Pacific "Ring of Fire," is one of the world's most disaster-prone countries but has never had an agency dedicated to disaster management.
Instead, the country has relied on temporary response teams assembled from different government ministries and departments.

As part of the launch, the agency urged local governments and residents to check the quake resistance of their homes, make sure their furniture is safely anchored, evaluate their evacuation procedures and stock up on emergency supplies.

The agency was not established in response to any specific threat, but amid concerns about Japan's ability to cope with another crisis on the scale of the 2011 quake and tsunami, which killed nearly 20,000 people, and triggered the Fukushima nuclear disaster.
Experts have warned of the possibility of major quakes in the coming decades and officials want people to be prepared.
The biggest worry is a megaquake along the Nankai Trough, an undersea trench off Japan's southeastern coast.
According to government estimates, such a disaster could kill 298,000 people, force 6.5 million to evacuate and destroy 2.35 million homes.

A major earthquake in metropolitan Tokyo could cause another 18,000 deaths, while an eruption of Mount Fuji could affect 790,000 people and disrupt transportation, power lines and other infrastructure.

Japan has long been criticized for its poorly equipped evacuation centers, where people are typically crowded into gymnasiums, community centers and classrooms that lack adequate privacy, bedding, clean toilets or hot food.
The new agency aims to change that by bringing in clean portable toilets, kitchens serving hot food, bathing facilities and cardboard beds.

The importance of better shelters became clear after the 2011 disaster, when {{prn:3,810|three thousand eight hundred and ten}} people died from causes linked to harsh living conditions following the earthquake and tsunami.

articles.title: UK Airline Offers to Pay for Babies' First Passports
articles.intro: Learn about a UK airline offering to cover the cost of babies' first passports, parental travel experiences, and family vacation milestones.

sentences.text: The end of September is the busiest time for births in the UK.
And with so many new babies in the country, one company is already hoping to turn some of them into customers — and get them on a plane!

British airline and vacation company Easyjet has announced that it will cover the cost of a child's passport when new parents book a trip — or, at least, give parents a discount that will cover the passport cost.
Until November 26, 2026, parents of babies will be able to save about $90 on Easyjet trips, which is the same as the price of a child's first passport in the UK.
They can use the offer once per vacation booking for one child up to 2 years old.
Easyjet also surveyed 2,000 British parents who had taken a child under 5 on vacation at least once about their experiences.
Four out of five parents said their baby's first vacation was a "landmark family moment," with 57% saying it was one of their proudest parenting milestones.
They were also asked about the difficult parts of organizing international travel with a new baby.
And nearly one in 10 said they didn't even know their baby needed their own passport before they started planning their vacation!
Parents also said it took an average of four tries to get a passport picture approved for their baby — after all, you can't tell a baby how to pose for a photo!
Still, 48% said their baby's first vacation was easier than they had expected, and 87% said they felt good about doing it all again.
Also, even though 27% said they thought it would be difficult for small children to adapt to a new routine on vacation, 50% said their children were actually able to do so quite well.

articles.title: Sardinian Restaurants Ask Families to Put Phones Away
articles.intro: This lesson explores Sardinian restaurants asking families to put away electronic devices at meals to encourage conversation and quality time together.

sentences.text: Going out for a meal with your family should be a chance to enjoy good food and spend time together.
But these days, it's common to see everyone looking at their phones or watching videos on tablets instead of talking.
Now, some restaurants on the Italian island of Sardinia are trying to change that.

Starting in early November, 15 restaurants are encouraging parents and children to put away their phones and other electronic devices during meals, so they can spend more time talking and enjoying their meals together.
The project, called "At the Table Without Screens," will run for one month at first, and more restaurants may join later.
Families visiting these restaurants can choose whether to take part in the project.
Those who agree are asked to leave their devices in their bags or put them in a basket at the table.
But the restaurants aren't just asking families to stop using their phones — they're also giving them something else to do.
Families receive a special kit with games, drawing activities and other things to help parents and children talk more.
They can play games while waiting for their food, or use the activities as a starting point for conversations.
The kit also includes advice for parents on children's screen time and social media use at home.
The project is led by Anna Cau, Sardinia's children's ombudsman.
She believes parents need more support to help their children use technology safely.
Emanuele Frongia, the head of a restaurant association in Sardinia, says dining out should be a time for families to talk and enjoy each other's company.
"But adults must set a good example first," he said.
"We can't ask children to put away their phones if we're not willing to do the same."

articles.title: 80% of Netflix Users Have Watched Korean Content
articles.intro: Explore the global rise of Korean dramas on Netflix, their international popularity, and how subtitles and dubbing boost their worldwide appeal.

sentences.text: Have you ever watched a Korean drama on Netflix?
If you have, you're certainly not alone!
According to Netflix, about 80% of its subscribers around the world have watched at least one Korean show or movie.
It's been 10 years since Netflix arrived in South Korea in 2016.
And since then, Korean entertainment has become popular in many different parts of the world.
Since 2021, Netflix has shared weekly lists of its 10 most-watched shows and movies around the world, called the "Global Top 10."
More than 210 different Korean shows and movies have appeared on these lists.
One of the biggest hits has been _Squid Game_.
The series stayed on Netflix's Global Top 10 for 32 weeks, including nine weeks at number one.
But it's not just _Squid Game_ that's getting attention from people around the world.
In Japan, _Crash Landing on You_, a 2019 story about a South Korean woman who falls in love with a North Korean soldier, stayed in the country's Top 10 for 72 weeks.
In Bolivia, the 2009 show _Boys Over Flowers_ spent 49 weeks in the Top 10, while 2021's _Vincenzo_ stayed in Pakistan's Top 10 for 45 weeks.
One reason these shows have become so popular is that they're available in different languages.
For example, the third season of _Squid Game_, released in 2025, was available with subtitles in 37 languages.
People could also watch dubbed versions of the show in 24 languages.
So 10 years after Netflix arrived in South Korea, Korean entertainment is popular in countries all over the world.

The survey comes at a time when many people in Malaysia are struggling with the rising cost of living.

articles.title: These US Cities Spend the Most on Groceries
articles.intro: Explore which US cities spend the most and least on groceries, and how prices and household income affect grocery budgets.

sentences.text: Grocery prices are rising around the world.
There are many reasons for this, including rising fuel costs, climate change and global instability, and the exact rise in prices can be very different depending on where you live.
Finance app WalletHub has put together a list of cities where Americans are spending the most and least amount of their money on groceries.
It looked at the prices of 26 common grocery items across 100 of the largest US cities.
It added up the cost of those items and compared that with the average household income in each city, to see where people are spending the largest share of their money at the grocery store.
Detroit, Michigan, is at the top of the list, with residents needing to spend more than 4% of the city's average household income to buy the 26 common grocery items.
Fremont, California, has the lowest spending as a percentage of income, at less than 1%.
That doesn't mean Detroit has the highest overall prices, though.
Looking at the specific prices of those 26 grocery items, Detroit is actually just the 39th most expensive city.
However, the city has the lowest average annual household income in America, at just under $40,000 — while Fremont's is over $160,000.
This means people in Detroit have to spend a higher percentage of their income on groceries compared to people in higher-earning cities.
The situation is similar in Cleveland, Ohio, where residents spend the second-largest percentage of their income on groceries — just under 4%.
Cleveland actually has relatively low prices for a number of items on the grocery list, but it also has the second-lowest average household income, at just under $41,000 per year.
Birmingham, Alabama, is in third place, with residents needing to spend 3.5% of their average $46,000 income on groceries.

articles.title: Study Finds How a High-Calorie Diet May Affect the Brain
articles.intro: Explore recent research on how high-calorie diets can harm brain function, impact cognitive health, and what might reverse these effects.

sentences.text: We already know that high-calorie diets can cause obesity and are linked with illnesses like type 2 diabetes.
But there is growing evidence that these diets may affect healthy brain function as well.
Studies have, in particular, linked high-calorie diets with poorer cognitive performance and an increased risk of conditions like Alzheimer's disease.
To better understand what may be causing this, researchers from the Institute of Science Tokyo looked at the effect of a high-calorie diet on mice.
Their study, published in _Molecular Psychiatry_, revealed how a high-calorie diet could be linked to altered brain function and cognitive impairment.
The researchers fed mice a diet that was high in fat — which is incredibly calorie-dense — for either one or six weeks.
Then they compared the nerve cells of these mice with those that ate a normal diet.
They found that the mice on a high-fat diet had reduced levels of a protein called PQBP1 in their cerebral cortex — an area of the brain that supports cognitive functioning.
PQBP1 regulates the production of other proteins that are necessary for the brain's nerve cells to work properly.
When they looked closer, the researchers found that higher levels of insulin — a hormone that manages blood sugar levels — among the mice on a high-fat diet had restricted the production of PQBP1.
The result was an overall decline in healthy brain activity.
However, the researchers also found a way to reverse this damage, which may have positive implications for human health too.
Some mice that were fed a high-fat diet were also treated with pioglitazone, a drug used for diabetes management.
The researchers found that the medication brought PQBP1 levels back to normal, and improved cognitive function.
They also had success in using gene therapy to restore PQBP1 and fix brain function problems.
So, while the study revealed the potential dangers of a high-calorie diet for brain health, it also found possible effective approaches for treating some of the negative impacts.

articles.title: Accent Change May Be Sign of a Good Ear — Study
articles.intro: Explore a study on how people’s accents can change when exposed to others and what this reveals about listening skills and language perception.

sentences.text: If you spend time with someone who speaks with a different accent than you, you may start to sound like them.
Or they may start to sound like you!
But no matter how much time you spend together, you both probably won't sound exactly the same — and researchers aren't sure why.
A new study looked at 136 people who speak English with an American accent.
They were first asked to read a list of words aloud.
Next, they were told to listen to a recording of a woman saying the same words with an Australian accent.
The participants were then asked to read the words aloud again.
However, they received three different types of instructions.
Some were told to read in their normal accent.
Some were told to imitate the Australian speaker as closely as possible.
And some received no instruction.
The results showed that people could copy the Australian accent when asked to.
And when told to speak normally, most people kept their American accent.
However, those who received no instruction tended to copy just one part of the Australian accent — dropping the "r" sound in certain words.
Participants were also asked what they noticed about the woman's accent.
The most common answers were the way she pronounced the letter "r," and the vowel sound in words like "bath."
The researchers found that participants who noticed these sounds tended to copy them more.
This was true whether they had been asked to imitate the woman or had received no instructions.

"Basically, if we don't tell you whether or not to imitate somebody, you're going to sound like them on the bits that you notice or think are interesting," researcher Kathryn Campbell-Kibler explained.
So maybe if your accent changes more than others', it means your ears notice those differences more!

articles.title: 31% of Japan's Graduates Quit Jobs Within 3 Years
articles.intro: Explore why many young Japanese graduates leave their jobs within three years, changing attitudes toward lifetime employment, and related workforce trends.

sentences.text: In Japan, it was once common for people to work at the same company for their whole career.
This tradition, known as _shushin koyo_, or "lifetime employment," became popular after World War II.
Companies offered workers secure jobs, and workers often stayed until they retired.
But lifetime employment is no longer as common as it once was, and these days, many young Japanese workers leave their jobs after just a few years.
According to a new government survey, 31% of people who graduated from university in March 2023 left their jobs within three years.
And in some industries, the number was much higher.
For example, 50% of university graduates working in the accommodation and food services sector left within three years.
And in education, it was 42%.
Company size also made a big difference.
At large companies with at least 1,000 workers, about one in four young employees left within three years.
But at companies with fewer than five workers, almost 60% of employees left.
And it's not just university graduates — 37% of high school graduates also left their jobs within three years.
However, the survey also found that fewer young people are leaving their jobs than before.
In fact, this is the second year the number has fallen.
One reason may be that companies are trying harder to keep their employees.
As Japan's population gets older, there are fewer workers available, so some companies are offering higher pay and better working conditions to encourage people to stay.
Japan's tradition of lifetime employment may no longer be as common as it once was, but companies are still finding ways to encourage young workers to stay longer.

It included 1,000 people aged 19 to 34, all of whom were looking for work at the time of the survey.
It found that nearly 70% feel financially strained because they spend a lot of money doing things that will help them get a job.
Certifications and language tests are the top expenses, the survey found, followed by general education costs and study materials.
People who have been preparing for employment for three years or more were found to spend an average of 800,000 won, or about $600, each month.

Those aged 30 to 34 were found to spend an average of 600,000 won — about $450 — each month, while those aged 19 to 24 spend 560,000 won, or about $420.

Those hoping to work for very large companies also spend more than the average.
The survey also found that 33% of participants get financial help from their families to cover these costs.
Another 30% use money they get from part-time jobs or other work.
When asked what kind of support would help them most, a quarter said they want financial help with certification and language test costs.

sentences.text: What annoys you most when you're out in public?
People being rude?
Someone pushing ahead of you in a line?
Or perhaps someone using their phone's speaker in public?
A new survey shows that British people have a lot to complain about.
The survey, done by YouGov, asked more than 2,000 people across the UK what bothers them about other people when they're in public.
The biggest complaint was people being rude to shop and restaurant workers, which annoys 67% of people who took the survey.
People who don't wait their turn in a line came second, at 59%.
Other common problems included people using their phone speakers in public, people taking up too much space on streets or buses and trains, and people making videos of themselves for social media.
But while these things bother people, they aren't actually the things they complain about most.
In fact, when asked what they complain about most in everyday life, 24% chose things they see in the news.
Another 18% chose people being rude — so that's on both lists — while 11% chose work.
And although British people are famous for talking about the country's bad weather, only 6% said the weather was what they complain about most.
And just 8% chose traffic.

articles.title: Young Japanese Have Worse Diets than Older Japanese
articles.intro: This lesson explores a study comparing the diets of young and older Japanese people, highlighting health, nutrition, and lifestyle factors.

sentences.text: A new study has found that young adults in Japan often have less healthy diets than older people in the country.
Researchers from the University of Tokyo did a study with about 4,500 people in Japan.
The people were as old as 79, and as young as just 1.
The researchers asked them — or their parents — to write down what they ate and drank for eight days.
Then, they gave them diet scores.
The researchers looked at two things: the foods people ate, like fruit and vegetables, and the nutrients they got, like vitamins.
Men who were around 23 years old, and women who were around 16, had the lowest scores for the foods they ate.
After that, their scores got better almost every year they got older.
For nutrients, both men's and women's scores went up until around age 10.
But then they went down quickly, until they were at their lowest around age 24.
After that, nutrient scores started slowly going up again.
The study also found that people from families with more money and education had healthier diets.
And smokers and people who skip breakfast in the morning had less healthy diets.
The researchers said teens and young adults may find it harder to eat well because their lives are changing so much at that age.
But they said it's important to teach young people how to eat healthily.

articles.title: Money-Smart Friends Could Save You $500 a Year
articles.intro: This lesson explores how having friends with financial expertise can help you save money and highlights the value of diverse skills in friend groups.

sentences.text: Every friend group has its experts — the one who always knows good places to eat, the one who can fix your computer, and perhaps the one everyone turns to for money advice.
That last friend could be especially useful.
According to a new survey by Talker Research, Americans who follow money advice from friends say it saves them an average of $482 a year.
One in seven said a friend's advice had saved them more than $800.
The survey of 2,000 Americans found that 35% think every friend group needs someone who is good with money.
Among those who have such a friend, nearly a third said they ask that person for advice all the time.
And one in six believe they're the money expert in their own group.
So what kind of advice are friends sharing?
People most often helped their friends with advice on how to improve their credit scores, how to do their taxes and how to invest.
But having the right group of friends can come in handy for more than just money advice.
Forty-one percent said their ideal friend group would include a mechanic, while 32% wanted a doctor and 29% a lawyer.
Overall, eight in ten agreed that it's useful to have friends who are good at different things, and one in five said they turn to their friends for help all the time.
